strings.name: Kate Raworth
strings.role: Economist and co-founder of Doughnut Economics Action Lab
strings.summary: Kate Raworth is a British economist who developed the Doughnut framework connecting basic social needs with planetary ecological boundaries. She previously contributed to research at UNDP and Oxfam, published Doughnut Economics in 2017, and co-founded an action lab to help cities, businesses and communities explore applications.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Conceptual frameworks, indicator measurements and policy effects are distinguished, as are appointments, honorary degrees and co-authors' contributions; publication dates are not recording dates.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed the Doughnut Economics framework, combining social needs and ecological boundaries in discussions of development.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Oxford BA in Philosophy, Politics and Economics and MSc in Economics for Development; honorary doctorates are not treated as earned doctorates.
strings.facts.f2.label: Teaching and practice
strings.facts.f2.value: Her biography lists Senior Teaching Fellow at Oxford's Environmental Change Institute and Professor of Practice at Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences; the latter is not an Oxford professorship.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Social foundation and ecological ceiling
strings.highlights.h1.text: The framework focuses on a safe space between unmet basic needs and ecological overshoot, proposing that progress be assessed through both human wellbeing and planetary boundaries.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Collaborative research and local application
strings.highlights.h2.text: She updated the indicator framework with Andrew Fanning and worked with teams to apply these ideas in cities and organisations; adopting a tool does not mean its goals have been achieved.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Economics interview released
strings.timeline.t1.text: In an interview published by Leyla Acaroglu, she discussed economic goals, social needs and systemic change; the date records publication.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Updated boundaries study co-published
strings.timeline.t2.text: With Andrew Fanning, she published a Nature study using 35 indicators to examine social shortfall and ecological overshoot during 2000–2022.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Delivers Macaulay lecture
strings.timeline.t3.text: The organiser's retrospective confirms that she delivered the 46th TB Macaulay Lecture in Edinburgh.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Amsterdam City Doughnut launched
strings.timeline.t4.text: An international team adapted the global framework into a city analysis tool; this does not mean the city had achieved all sustainability goals.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Inaugurated as Professor of Practice
strings.timeline.t5.text: Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences held an inauguration and invited her to contribute to curriculum and practical exploration.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Co-founds the action lab
strings.timeline.t6.text: Doughnut Economics Action Lab launched, connecting the framework with practitioners' experiments.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Publishes Doughnut Economics
strings.timeline.t7.text: The book explores renewed economic thinking through seven approaches, without prescribing a single policy recipe for every place.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Oxfam discussion paper published
strings.timeline.t8.text: A Safe and Just Space for Humanity connected social needs and planetary boundaries in a doughnut-shaped diagram.
